chi-comanda.domanda: Find out who you are and which groups you belong to. Then use sudo to act as root: ask who you are and read the file of encrypted passwords.
obiettivi: Show user and groups with id
suggerimenti: The first command has two letters. For the other two you need to write sudo in front of the command.
Try cat /etc/shadow without sudo first: you'll see permission denied. Then add sudo in front.
Run id, then sudo whoami (it answers root), then sudo cat /etc/shadow.
chi-comanda.spiegazione: With sudo the command runs as root, which passes every permission check: that's why sudo whoami answers root and sudo cat /etc/shadow can read a file forbidden to other users.

porta-chiusa.domanda: You type touch /etc/prova and get: touch: cannot touch '/etc/prova': Permission denied. Why?

opzioni.di-root: The /etc folder belongs to root and a normal user can't create files in it.
opzioni.nome-sbagliato: The name “prova” isn't allowed on Linux.

feedback.non-esiste: If /etc didn't exist the message would say No such file or directory.
feedback.disco-pieno: With a full disk the message would be No space left on device.
feedback.nome-sbagliato: “prova” is a valid name: the problem is where you're trying to create it.

suggerimenti: Permission denied means you're not allowed.
Who owns system folders like /etc?
/etc belongs to root: the student can't create files in it. With sudo touch /etc/prova it would work.
porta-chiusa.spiegazione: System folders belong to root. A normal user can read them but not change them: it's a protection. To change something there you need sudo.

leggi-permessi.domanda: A file has these permissions: -rw-r----- 1 studente contabili ... bilancio.txt. Who can read it?

opzioni.proprietario-gruppo: The student (owner) and anyone in the contabili group.
opzioni.nessuno: Nobody, because the x permission is missing.

feedback.tutti: The last triplet, the others', is ---: anyone who isn't the owner or in the group can't do anything.
feedback.solo-proprietario: The group triplet is r--: people in the contabili group can read.
feedback.nessuno: x is for running a program, not for reading a file.

suggerimenti: Split the permissions into three triplets after the first character: rw- / r-- / ---.
The first triplet is the owner's, the second the group's, the third the others'. Where does the r appear?
The r is in the owner's triplet and the group's: the student and the contabili group can read.
leggi-permessi.spiegazione: rw- (owner: reads and writes), r-- (group: reads), --- (others: nothing). So the owner and the contabili group can read.

numero-permessi.modello: The permissions rwxr-xr-x written as numbers are ___ .
feedbackSpazi: Work out one digit per triplet: r = 4, w = 2, x = 1.
suggerimenti: Split into three triplets: rwx, r-x, r-x.
The answer is 755.
numero-permessi.spiegazione: rwx = 7, r-x = 5, r-x = 5: 755. It's the typical permission of programs and scripts: everyone can run them, only the owner modifies them.

primo-script.domanda: Your folder has the saluta.sh script, but it won't start. Make it executable and run it. Then protect segreto.txt so only you can read and modify it.
suggerimenti: Look at the permissions with ls -l. To change them you need chmod.
chmod u+x saluta.sh adds execute for the owner. For segreto.txt: rw- = 6, --- = 0.
Type chmod u+x saluta.sh, then ./saluta.sh, then chmod 600 segreto.txt (or chmod go-r segreto.txt).
primo-script.spiegazione: A script needs the x permission to be started with ./. With 600 (rw-------) a file can be read and modified only by its owner: it's the right permission for files with passwords and keys.

installa-tree.domanda: The tree command isn't installed. Update the package list, install it and use it to see the structure of your folders.
suggerimenti: Installing programs is an administrator operation: you need sudo.
The commands are sudo apt update and sudo apt install followed by the package name.
Type sudo apt update, then sudo apt install tree, then tree.
installa-tree.spiegazione: apt update refreshes the list, apt install downloads and installs the package from the repository. Both need sudo; using the installed program doesn't.

ordine-apt.domanda: Put in order the steps to install and use a new program.
suggerimenti: Before choosing from the catalog, it's worth having an up-to-date catalog.
A program can only be used after it's installed.
The order is: sudo apt update, sudo apt install tree, tree.
ordine-apt.spiegazione: First you refresh the package list, then you install, finally you use the program. You'll find the same order again in Dockerfiles.

crea-variabile.domanda: Create a COLORE variable with the value blu, put it in the environment and check it with printenv.
obiettivi: The environment variable COLORE is blu
Show its value with printenv COLORE
suggerimenti: Remember: name, equals and value, all together. To put it in the environment you need one more command.
export COLORE=blu creates the variable and exports it at the same time.
Type export COLORE=blu and then printenv COLORE (it must print blu).
crea-variabile.spiegazione: export puts the variable in the environment, so programs started by the shell, such as printenv, receive it too. Without export, printenv wouldn't have seen it.

cosa-e-path.domanda: What does the PATH variable contain?

opzioni.cartelle-programmi: The list of folders where the shell looks for programs.
opzioni.cartella-corrente: The path of the folder you're in.
opzioni.cronologia: The list of commands already run.

feedback.cartella-corrente: The current folder is in PWD, not in PATH.
feedback.cronologia: History is shown with history and saved in .bash_history.
feedback.password: Passwords are never kept in system environment variables.

suggerimenti: Try echo $PATH in the lesson's terminal: what do you see?
They're folder paths separated by colons.
PATH contains the folders where the shell looks for programs when you type a command.
cosa-e-path.spiegazione: When you type a command, the shell looks for it in the folders listed in PATH, in order. If the program is somewhere else, you get command not found.

caccia-agli-errori.domanda: An application's log contains INFO and ERRORE (error) messages. Save only the error lines in a file errori.txt and count how many there are.
obiettivi: Save the lines with ERRORE to the file ~/errori.txt
suggerimenti: grep keeps only the lines containing some text. With > you send the result to a file.
grep ERRORE registro.log > errori.txt saves the errors. To count them use wc -l on the file, or a pipe.
Type grep ERRORE registro.log > errori.txt and then wc -l errori.txt (or grep ERRORE registro.log | wc -l).
caccia-agli-errori.spiegazione: grep filters lines, > saves output to a file, wc -l counts lines. By connecting simple programs with redirection and pipes you do complex analyses: that's how container logs are read.

dove-va-errore.domanda: You run ls documenti nulla > elenco.txt. The documenti folder exists, nulla doesn't. Where does the error message about nulla appear?

opzioni.schermo: On the screen, because > only redirects standard output.
opzioni.file: In the elenco.txt file, together with the listing.
opzioni.entrambi: Both on the screen and in the file.

feedback.file: > only concerns standard output: errors travel on standard error.
feedback.nessuno: To throw them away you'd need 2> /dev/null.
feedback.entrambi: Each message goes on one channel only: the error is on standard error.

suggerimenti: Every program has two separate outputs: one for results and one for errors.
> only redirects one of the two. Which one?
On the screen: > only sends standard output to the file, while the error travels on standard error.
dove-va-errore.spiegazione: Standard output (the listing) ends up in the file, standard error (the message about nulla) stays on the screen. To send errors to the file too you add 2>&1.

ferma-il-ribelle.domanda: The computer is very slow: a program is using almost the whole processor. Find it and stop it.
obiettivi: The calcolo-infinito process must no longer be running
suggerimenti: ps aux shows all processes with the %CPU column: look for the one with the highest value and note its PID.
Try kill followed by the PID first. If the process is still there, check with ps aux and use the stronger signal.
With ps aux you'll find python3 calcolo-infinito.py and its PID. kill PID isn't enough, because it ignores TERM: you need kill -9 PID.
ferma-il-ribelle.spiegazione: kill sends TERM, a request to close that this process ignores. kill -9 sends KILL, which the kernel enforces anyway: it's the remedy to use only when the polite request doesn't work.

segnale-giusto.domanda: You need to stop a program that is saving data. What's the right way to proceed?

opzioni.prima-term: First kill PID (TERM), and kill -9 only if it doesn't close.
opzioni.subito-kill: Straight away kill -9 PID, it's faster.

feedback.subito-kill: KILL doesn't give the program time to finish saving: you risk half-written data.
feedback.ctrl-c: Ctrl+C only sends a signal to the foreground program in that terminal.
feedback.riavvia: Restarting stops everything, even what was working: it's far more drastic than needed.

suggerimenti: Think of the difference between asking to close and pulling the plug.
Which signal lets the program finish what it's doing?
First kill PID, which sends TERM and lets it close in an orderly way; kill -9 only if it doesn't respond.
segnale-giusto.spiegazione: TERM asks the process to close and gives it time to save. KILL stops it instantly. Docker does the same with docker stop: first TERM, then KILL after 10 seconds.
